item.title: More math typesetting
item.description:
For some reason, new paragraphs are started after a display equation, even when I don’t want them to. That’s ok for now. Anyways, what’s \(\abs{x + 1}\)? Here’s a fun fact, \(\comm{x}{p} = -i \, \hbar\), and that \(\innerprod{j}{k} = \delta_{j k}\).

Here’s some math typesetting stuff. For starters I’ll just write down the Linblad equation, a nice bit of physics for open quantum systems,

$$\diffp{\rho}{t} = \sum_j \gamma_j \left( L_j \, \rho(t) \, L_j^\dagger -\frac{1}{2} \lbrace L_j^\dagger L_j, \rho(t)\rbrace\right) -\lbrack H, \rho(t) \rbrack \,.$$

Hello \(x\). This is my fun Skibbidi test. For some reason certain things I do just make paragraphs disappear. Why is the web like this? Do you know what it takes to make me miss the strength and certainty of TeX?
